card.what: Forged stainless long D (dee) shackle, 5 mm pin with a flat key head, as on Bean's sheet: the shackle for a straight pull
card.boats: J/22 jib sheets to the clew, the vang and mainsheet blocks to their bails, the spinnaker sheets; the Sunfish's mainsheet block
card.distance: arm's reach in the cockpit and at the clew
card.before: kit ShackleD (Oct 2026): one bent tube, a plain pin and a round head, 29 mm, pin along Y; used by no layout yet

references.use: the look: two key-pin D shackles at three-quarter view (not square-on: proportions not measured)
references.url: Bean's hardware reference sheet (project upload, Nov 8 2026), bottom row 'Dee Shakles'
references.licence: for measuring and look only; never committed or shared

references.use: square-on D shackle with a key-head pin (a heavy galvanised lifting D, much fatter than a sailing one): the key head, ears and pin only, not proportions

references.note: 5 mm forged stainless self-locking long D shackle (Wichard 1212 class, as on Bean's sheet): L 41 mm overall, A 29 mm inside length, B 10 mm opening, G 26 mm (S3i table). The standard D (1202) is 29 mm overall

sizes.name: Width with the key head
sizes.source: reported only (20 mm across the legs plus the key head)

features.text: Straight parallel legs and a half-round crown, long (inside length about three times the opening)
Forged 5 mm body with a flat section (flat faces, rounded edges), one piece with its ears
Two flat round ears at the pin, growing out of the legs
5 mm pin right through both ears
Flat key head on one end of the pin, with a hole for seizing wire
Collar between the key head and the ear
Rounded pin end just proud of the far ear
10 mm opening between the ears (takes a 10 mm line's thimble or a block's eye)

budget.note: hero is a Nanite part; a shackle is small, so the build aims at about 13k
